packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1 confidence 100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs after attendee insertion has committed, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted without invitations and a retry is rejected by the existing-attendee filter before it can repair synchronization.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:94 — [P1 confidence 100] `id: bookingId,` is the only write predicate and no booking-status check precedes it, allowing cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings to acquire guests and emit the new templates' unconditional CONFIRMED calendar invitations.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:56 — [P3 confidence 100] `setIsInvalidEmail(true);` has no corresponding reset on editing, successful validation, success, or `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so an invalid submission leaves the error visible after correction and subsequent reopening unless the user explicitly clicks Cancel.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P2 confidence 100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares an unnormalized guest against lowercase blacklist entries, allowing a caller to bypass the configured block with an uppercase domain such as blocked@EXAMPLE.COM and send the invitation to the same mailbox.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P2 confidence 75] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts arbitrarily many copies of a previously absent address, which the handler inserts individually and the email manager sends individually, allowing an authorized attendee to amplify one request into repeated invitations to a victim mailbox despite the client-only uniqueness check.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [P1 confidence 75] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` initializes the calendar updater with the requesting attendee's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so an explicitly allowed attendee cannot reliably update the organizer's external calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` gets the credentials of the requesting user (ctx.user), not the booking organizer. Looking at the code, the permission check allows attendees to add guests (line 48: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`). When an attendee adds guests, `ctx.user` is the attendee, not the organizer. The EventManager is then initialized with the attendee's credentials, but the calendar event belongs to the organizer. This means when an attendee adds guests, the calendar update would use the attendee's credentials instead of the organizer's credentials, which would fail to update the organizer's external calendar. This is a real bug in the logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1 confidence 100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs after attendee insertion has committed, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted without invitations and a retry is rejected by the existing-attendee filter before it can repair synchronization.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real atomicity issue. Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts, the flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update() commits new attendees to the database (lines 89-103), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees() is called (line 165), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails() is called (line 169). If step 2 fails (calendar API error), the attendees are already persisted in the database. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will filter out these already-added attendees since they now exist in booking.attendees, causing the retry to fail with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This leaves the system in an inconsistent state where guests exist in the database but weren't added to the calendar. This is a legitimate consistency/atomicity bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:94 — [P1 confidence 100] `id: bookingId,` is the only write predicate and no booking-status check precedes it, allowing cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings to acquire guests and emit the new templates' unconditional CONFIRMED calendar invitations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the booking query at line 27-44 fetches the booking with `where: { id: bookingId }` and includes attendees, eventType, etc. The code then checks permissions (isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee) but there is NO check for booking.status. The code proceeds to add guests to the booking regardless of whether the booking is cancelled, rejected, pending, or any other status. This means guests can be added to cancelled bookings, and the email templates send CONFIRMED calendar invitations unconditionally. This is a real logic bug - the handler should verify the booking is in an appropriate status (like ACCEPTED/CONFIRMED) before allowing guests to be added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence 100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes an event without any team property, making the email manager's team-member notification branch unreachable for this endpoint and omitting collective hosts from organizer notifications.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the `evt` object constructed in addGuests.handler.ts does not include a `team` property. In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts lines 522-548), there's a check `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)` that iterates over team members to send them OrganizerAddGuestsEmail. Since `evt.team` is undefined, this branch will never execute, meaning team members won't receive notification emails when guests are added. This is a real bug - the code structure suggests team member notifications were intended (the email manager has the logic), but the handler doesn't populate the team data needed to trigger it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence 100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` discards delivery failures and then returns success without a retry record, leaving newly persisted guests permanently uninformed because resubmitting the same addresses is rejected as already present.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in addGuests.handler.ts lines 168-171, when sendAddGuestsEmails fails, the error is caught and only logged with console.log, but the function still returns success ({message: 'Guests added'}). The guests have already been persisted to the database (line 85-98), so if the user tries to add the same guests again, they would be filtered out as duplicates (line 71-74). This means guests could be added to the booking but never receive notification emails, with no way to retry. This is a real correctness/reliability issue - silent failure of email delivery with no recovery mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:56 — [P3 confidence 100] `setIsInvalidEmail(true);` has no corresponding reset on editing, successful validation, success, or `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so an invalid submission leaves the error visible after correction and subsequent reopening unless the user explicitly clicks Cancel.

adjudication.rationale:
Looking at the code, the finding claims that `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` has no reset on editing, successful validation, success, or dialog reopening. Let's verify:

1. In `handleAdd()`, when validation succeeds, the mutation is called but `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is NOT called before the mutation.
2. In `onSuccess`, `setIsInvalidEmail` is NOT reset - only `setMultiEmailValue([''])` and `setIsOpenDialog(false)` are called.
3. In the Cancel button's onClick, `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` IS called along with other resets.
4. When the dialog is reopened via `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, there's no reset of `isInvalidEmail`.
5. When the user edits the email values (via `setValue={setMultiEmailValue}`), `isInvalidEmail` is NOT reset.

So if a user: (1) enters invalid email, (2) clicks Add, (3) sees error, (4) fixes the email, (5) clicks Add again - the validation would pass and mutation would fire, but the error message would still be visible until the mutation succeeds. More importantly, if the user closes the dialog via clicking outside (which triggers `onOpenChange`) instead of Cancel, and reopens it, the error state persists.

This is a real UI bug - the error state is not properly cleared in several scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P2 confidence 75] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts arbitrarily many copies of a previously absent address, which the handler inserts individually and the email manager sends individually, allowing an authorized attendee to amplify one request into repeated invitations to a victim mailbox despite the client-only uniqueness check.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the schema in addGuests.schema.ts, it accepts `z.array(z.string().email())` without any uniqueness constraint. The handler in addGuests.handler.ts does filter for uniqueness against existing attendees with `uniqueGuests.filter(...)`, but it does NOT deduplicate the input array itself. If someone passes `['victim@example.com', 'victim@example.com', 'victim@example.com']`, all three would pass the filter (since none are existing attendees), all three would be inserted as separate attendees via `createMany`, and then `sendAddGuestsEmails` would send emails to all of them. The client-side validation in AddGuestsDialog.tsx uses a Zod schema with `.refine()` to check uniqueness, but this is client-only and can be bypassed by calling the tRPC endpoint directly. This is a real server-side validation gap that could allow email amplification.
